subject.title: Vertex beta INVALID_ARGUMENT can wedge long sessions without actionable recovery

question: Should OpenClaw treat LiteLLM/Vertex beta generic 400 `INVALID_ARGUMENT` after long-session buildup as a recoverable provider/session error, and which recovery should be the default?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but generic `INVALID_ARGUMENT` covers multiple provider failure classes, so broad fallback, compaction, non-beta routing, or session rewriting needs maintainer intent and live provider proof.

options.title: Narrow provider-owned recovery
options.body: Add a LiteLLM/Vertex classifier for the verified error shape, surface actionable copy, preserve redacted diagnostics, and only trigger fallback/session cleanup where the provider contract proves it is safe.

options.title: Broader INVALID_ARGUMENT recovery
options.body: Classify more generic `INVALID_ARGUMENT` failures as recoverable across providers, accepting higher risk of misclassifying schema, media, auth, or route failures.

options.title: Hold for live repro only
options.body: Keep behavior unchanged until a live Vertex beta repro proves exact error metadata and lane state, delaying user recovery but avoiding speculative semantics.

recommendation.title: Narrow provider-owned recovery
recommendation.body: Add a LiteLLM/Vertex classifier for the verified error shape, surface actionable copy, preserve redacted diagnostics, and only trigger fallback/session cleanup where the provider contract proves it is safe.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has adjacent structured failover and LiteLLM plugin history and is the best available owner for the provider/fallback policy decision.
